messages:
dana: Quick idea for private control-plane onboarding: split the handshake into two explicit phases. Phase A = minimal auth + IP assignment (fast), Phase B = full feature negotiation + egress rule programming (slower). Goal: get agents reachable quickly and reduce long reconnect churn during onboarding. Thoughts?

liam: sounds promising. primary risk is inertia  agents thinking theyre fully ready after Phase A and sending traffic before routes/firewall rules exist. We need a canonical READY flag and SDK semantics.

nora: +1. also token issuance: phaseA should return a bootstrap token with very limited scope and a bounded lifetime. PhaseB exchanges for long-lived creds. Need offline refresh behavior if PhaseB stalls.

pat: operational concerns: what happens if PhaseB fails and we already created peering entries? we need a cleanup or safe-degrade path. Prefer idempotent apply semantics so retry doesn't double-provision routes.

dana: agree on idempotency. Proposal: PhaseA returns {ip, bootstrap_token, ready:false} and creates a tenancy record but does NOT advertise route tables to routers. PhaseB does the real programming and flips ready:true in control-plane state. SDKs observe ready:false and avoid sending production traffic, but can open health checks.

liam: can we lean on existing cert-manager for cert issuance in PhaseB? If cert issuance is async we should provide a webhook to notify control-plane when certs are ready, otherwise we need polling/backoff.

nora: webhook + exponential backoff as fallback. Also, for peering we should prefer keeping dataplane flow pinned to pre-provisioned NAT/ENI attachments so we don't thrash cloud route propagation. Document the sequence: attach ENI -> program SGs -> program routes -> flip ready.

pat: metrics we want: phaseA latency, phaseB latency, number of phaseB retries, queue depth for phaseB workers, and percentage of agents stuck at ready:false > X minutes. We'll need dashboards and alerts.

dana: rollout: feature-flag the PhaseB opt-in per-customer. Start with internal infra accounts, then a few low-risk customers. We'll run dual-handshake in parallel initially where agents perform both old handshake and new split and we reconcile differences.

liam: runtime change: if control-plane detects high contention on PhaseB worker pool, return 429 + Retry-After to agents for PhaseB attempts. PhaseA should still succeed so agent stays connected. That avoids thundering herd.

nora: SDK contract: when ready:false, SDK should only perform light telemetry and not attempt request routing. Also expose a backoff helper that respects 429 Retry-After and caps retries to N. We'll add a small code snippet in the SDK docs.

pat: ops playbook: on PhaseB backlog increase, manual mitigation = scale worker pool and temporarily divert new onboardings to a holding region. Also include steps to force-complete PhaseB for stuck tenants.

dana: infra-bot: please create ticket and stub playbook.

infra-bot: Created ticket NET-2081: "PhaseA/PhaseB control-plane handshake split + readiness gating". Playbook stub added at /ops/playbooks/phase-handshake.md. Assigned to @dana.

liam: thanks. next engineering tasks: write lightweight sequence diagram for the two-phase flow, implement idempotent apply for route programming, and add phaseB queue metrics. I'll take owner for queue/429 behavior.

nora: I'll prototype bootstrap token flow + refresh logic and draft SDK backoff helper.

pat: I'll draft the runbook and dashboard queries. Also add an alert for >5% agents stuck in ready:false for 10m.

dana: timeline: RFC addendum & diagrams this week, prototype in staging next sprint, limited customer canary after two sprints. Revisit if we see unexpected cross-region peering delays.

pat: small note: ensure we record audit events for phase transitions (cp.handshake.phaseA.completed, cp.handshake.phaseB.completed|failed) so SRE/SEC can trace partial onboarding.

liam: agree. we'll keep payloads small but include reason codes for failures (CERT_TIMEOUT, ROUTE_APPLY_FAIL, TOKEN_EXCHANGE_FAIL).

nora: one more thought: for air-gapped deployments we may never be able to run PhaseB asynchronously (cert authority constraints). We'll add an option to run PhaseB synchronously at deploy time via ops-run. Document that in addendum.

pat: perfect. that's enough to start. :thumbsup:
